A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same QP-SNN research work, with complete main text, references, and Appendices A–G. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support a reliable comparison of all 26 pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, object-detection, compression, and ablation results in Section 5, with additional empirical analyses in Appendices B, C, E, and F.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results, including classification comparisons in Table 1, detection results in Table 3, and supplementary analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The ReScaW quantization strategy, SVS pruning criterion, training procedure, and quantize-then-prune workflow are unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A and D.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, ImageNet-1k, and DVS-CIFAR10, plus object detection on SSDD and NWPU VHR-10. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1–7, including the cited compression methods, Spikingformer comparison, full-precision counterparts, and ablation baselines.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and Appendix G retain identical dataset splits, preprocessing, architectures, bit widths, timesteps, training budgets, pruning ratios, and evaluation metrics. Tables 8–11 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The scaling-coefficient comparison, component ablations, quantization/pruning-order experiment, efficiency analysis, and weight-distribution and kernel-score analyses are identical in Section 5.4 and Appendices B, C, E, and F.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests for the performance comparisons.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains 69.16% accuracy for the baseline and 73.89% with ReScaW and SVS; appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16 and their mathematical reasoning are unchanged, including bit-width utilization, quantization, singular-value scoring, gradient calculations, and the appendix definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about hardware-friendly compression, improved bit-width utilization, more reliable pruning, and competitive performance and efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of quantization efficiency, pruning robustness, and operation order are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same accuracy–compression tradeoff discussion, and Appendix G retains the qualification that pruning rates were manually selected.

D1.justification: The workflow, learning details, hyperparameters, architectures, pruning ratios, and model-size calculation remain identical in Appendices A, D, and G. No implementation or code/data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to earlier quantization and pruning research are unchanged. The edit in Section 2 only corrects spacing.

P1.justification: Section 2 changes 'However,these' to 'However, these'. The arXiv version/date stamp is also updated; wording, terminology, and document structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The spacing correction slightly reflows three lines in Section 2, and the first-page arXiv margin stamp changes. Figures 1–17 and Tables 1–11 retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement; all other pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes a missing space and updates the version stamp, without changing scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, or substantive presentation. These cosmetic differences do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
